inbox.title: Inbox
inbox.col.title: Title
new.title: New Proposal
proposal.generating: The agent is working on Article changes…
proposal.stale: Stale: this Article changed after the change was proposed.
proposal.codeStale: Cited code changed since this Proposal was drafted. Refresh it before revising or accepting.
proposal.submitHint: Decide on every change, then submit. Accepted changes become one commit.
bundles.title: Bundles
bundles.slugHint: Lowercase letters, digits and dashes, e.g. bl-kd
bundles.name: Display name
bundles.noArticles: No Articles yet. Accepted Proposals will appear here.
bundles.head: Latest commit
bundles.col.title: Title
proposal.reviseHint: Tell the agent what to change in this Article. Leave empty to just try again.
proposal.feedbackHint: e.g. "You missed the power section" or "Merge these into one Article". Accepted changes stay as they are.
proposal.noChanges: No changes left. Submit to close this Proposal, or send feedback to the agent.
settings.title: Settings
settings.claudeHint: Passed to claude --settings. Point it at your LLM endpoint here, e.g. {"env": {"ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL": "http://llm.intra:4000", "ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN": "..."}, "model": "..."}. Anyone who can open this page can read it.
new.titleHint: Defaults to the file name, page title or first line.
new.fileHint: PDF, Word, PowerPoint, Excel, HTML, text, or an image such as a photo of a handwritten note.
new.linkHint: A page or PDF on the intranet. Pages that need a login can't be fetched; save them as PDF and upload instead.
new.requestHint: Your statement is recorded with your name and cited by the Articles it changes.
new.codeFocus: What should the agent document from the code?
new.codeHint: The agent can read the Bundle's Reference directory: /references/{path}. Name the component or question to focus on.
new.codeMissing: Configure a Reference directory in this Bundle's Settings first.
settings.verifyCerts: Check TLS certificates when fetching links (off for intranet sites with private certificates)
new.textHint: Paste the content the knowledge should come from.
bundles.idPrefixHint: e.g. BK- gives new Articles BK-01, BK-02, …
bundles.cloneUrlHint: HTTP(S) URL or SSH URL, e.g. ssh://user@gerrit.intra:29418/project.git. SSH uses the worker's mounted key and known_hosts; tokens below are for HTTP(S).
bundles.referenceDirHint: Path below the read-only /references mount in the Docker worker, e.g. project-a. The agent can read this directory directly.
bundles.referenceExcludesHint: One glob per line. These guide the agent's search; they do not prevent reading a known file.
git.usernameHint: For a GitLab personal access token, leave blank to use oauth2. Otherwise enter the username associated with the token.
git.tokenHint: Used to clone, fetch and push over HTTP(S). For GitLab, use a token with write_repository access so accepted changes can be pushed.
git.tokenSaved: A token is saved. Leave blank to keep it, or enter a replacement.
git.removeToken: Remove the saved token when saving
git.newRemote: The repository URL has changed. Enter a token for the new URL if authentication is required.
bundles.branchHint: Leave empty for the repository's default branch.
bundles.rootHint: Where the Articles live, e.g. knowledge/bl-kd. Use . for the whole repository.
bundles.remoteHint: A git URL to back up every accepted change to, e.g. an empty GitLab project.
bset.name: Display name
bset.idFieldHint: Use dots for nested fields, e.g. cornerstone.knowledge_id
bset.index: Keep an Article table in index.md up to date
tmpl.intro: The Template tells the agent how Articles in this Bundle look. Changes are committed to .stonepedia/template.yaml.
mt.title: Maintenance
mt.check.integrityHint: Finds broken links, frontmatter that doesn't match the Template, missing or uncited Sources and duplicate ids. Produces a report; changes nothing.
mt.check.linksHint: Re-fetches linked pages that Articles cite. When a page changed, opens a Proposal to update those Articles.
mt.auditHint: Claude reviews every Article in the Bundle for duplicates, contradictions, broken cross-references and Template problems, and proposes fixes. The result is a normal Proposal you review.
welcome.title:
Good knowledge
deserves to
welcome.intro: Turn scattered documents into trusted knowledge. AI drafts the changes. Your team reviews them.
welcome.artAlt: Three balanced stones represent source material, human review, and lasting, git-versioned knowledge.
welcome.processIntro: Bring a source. Review the changes. Grow your Bundle.
welcome.step.sourceBody: Add a document, link, note, or request.
welcome.step.proposalBody: AI proposes changes using your sources and existing Articles.
welcome.step.reviewBody: Accept, revise, edit, or discard each change.
welcome.step.bundleBody: Accepted changes become git commits in your project’s Bundle.
welcome.preview.title: The release checklist
welcome.preview.source.label: 01 / SOURCE
welcome.preview.source.text: Before a release, verify the backup and record the rollback steps.
welcome.preview.proposal.label: 02 / PROPOSAL
welcome.preview.proposal.text: Verify the backup and document the rollback steps before each release.
welcome.preview.review.label: 03 / HUMAN REVIEW
welcome.preview.review.text: Verify the backup and document the rollback steps before each release.
welcome.preview.bundle.label: 04 / BUNDLE
welcome.preview.bundle.text: Verify the backup and document the rollback steps before each release.
welcome.maintenanceBody: Check for broken links, changed sources, and contradictions. Review suggested updates before accepting them.
welcome.ownershipBody: Each Bundle holds one project’s Articles and Sources. Keep them in Markdown, with history in your git repository.
welcome.agentsBody: Give your agents structured Articles, clear sources, and a consistent Template.
welcome.closingTitle:
What will your team
build on next?
